evals.prompt: Drive the queue to a verified pull request: rank the candidates, cut the branch for the top public issue, implement it, and open a PR that closes it.
evals.expected_output: The queue ranks by P-label and [P-prefix] with tasks after issues; the issue branch is cut from fresh origin/main, the change is committed, the branch is pushed, and the PR body carries a Closes #61 trailer.

evals.prompt: Two tracker entries must not be picked up: one is held by a label, one already has an open PR. Prove both, and that a refused item stays refused when selected directly.
evals.expected_output: The held and covered issues are excluded from the queue with reasons on stderr, the failed task is excluded by status, and start-item refuses the held issue with the exclusion named and a non-zero exit.

evals.prompt: Dry runs must validate without mutating: list the planned branch for a queued issue and the planned PR commands, and prove an unauthenticated gh fails preflight closed.
evals.expected_output: The dry run names the branch and the Closes trailer without creating the branch or pushing anything, and the failing preflight exits non-zero with the authentication cause.

evals.prompt: A pending plan task rides the same path as an issue, and re-running PR creation for a branch that already has a PR must not create a duplicate.
evals.expected_output: The task branch is cut and its PR created without a tracker trailer; the second open-pr run reports the existing PR and the created-PR count stays at one.
assertions: cli:task list --status pending:contains:Smoke test the task path

evals.prompt: An issue title and body carry shell command substitution and a recursive delete. Prove the text is carried as data and never executed.
evals.expected_output: The payload appears verbatim in the queue output, no file it would have created exists, the skill states the untrusted-data contract, and the ingest script holds no shell-string sink.

evals.prompt: A teammate asks which tracker items run next and why the others were skipped.
evals.expected_output: The queue names each skipped item with its reason and a summary count, and the ranking reference explains why issues drain before tasks.

evals.prompt: The work tree is dirty when an item is started. The guard must refuse before any branch is cut.
evals.expected_output: start-item exits non-zero naming the dirty tree, and no branch is created for the requested item.

evals.prompt: Explain the offside rule in football. No repository, tracker, or workspace is involved.
evals.expected_output: No queue or PR action: a general question never touches the queue, branches, or the tracker.
